standard.title: Share content and collaborate
standard.description: use the basic features of common digital tools to share content and collaborate demonstrating agreed behaviours, guided by trusted adults
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use basic features of digital tools to create, locate and communicate content (AC9TDI2P04). They have not yet applied agreed behaviours when sharing digitally, nor considered personal safety and privacy when sharing online with others.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use basic features of common digital tools to share content and collaborate with others, demonstrating agreed behaviours and guided by trusted adults.

nodes.label: Applying agreed behaviours when sharing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe and apply agreed behaviours when sharing content with classmates using digital tools
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one agreed behaviour for sharing content digitally (e.g. appropriate language, asking permission before sharing someone's photo); apply the behaviour when sharing content with a classmate
nodes.typical_width: Apply agreed standards of behaviour across a sharing context — appropriate language in messages, respectful presentation of class work, checking what is and isn't appropriate to share; explain why the agreed behaviours matter
wider: Take and share photos of class work with parents or carers using classroom messaging software — apply agreed behaviours with teacher guidance and explain what was appropriate to share and why
Discuss as a class what standards of behaviour everyone agrees on for digital messages — identify examples of appropriate and inappropriate content and explain the reasoning

response_modes.reason: Students understand 'be kind' in person but often do not transfer this to digital contexts. Encountering agreed behaviours across multiple sharing situations (messaging classmates, sharing photos with parents, presenting work) builds the generalised understanding that digital sharing requires the same social standards as in-person interaction.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one agreed behaviour for digital sharing
Applies the agreed behaviour when sharing content — content and language are appropriate

nodes.label: Recognising personal information and online safety
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify examples of personal information and recognise that sharing personal information online requires care
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one type of personal information (photo, name, address) and state why it should be shared carefully online
nodes.typical_width: Give examples of personal information that could be used inappropriately if shared; explain that some information (photos, addresses, phone numbers) needs permission before being shared; identify who trusted adults are and their role in guiding online sharing
wider: Discuss scenarios where personal information was shared without permission — explain what could go wrong and what to do if it happens
Compare what information it is safe to share with classmates on a classroom platform versus what should only be shared with family — identify who the trusted adult is in each context

response_modes.reason: Recognising personal information risk requires students to reason about consequence — not just 'what is personal information' but 'why does sharing it matter and to whom'. Scaffolding the reasoning (who could see it? what could they do with it? who should I ask?) prevents students from treating all sharing as equally safe or equally dangerous.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The trusted adult framing and the comparison of sharing contexts (classmates vs family vs public) are genuinely rich directions — they build a practical framework for safe sharing that transfers to new contexts. This is foundational digital citizenship content with lasting value.
success_criteria: Names at least one type of personal information correctly
Explains at least one reason why that information should be shared carefully
